raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

With `--api-server-count N > 1`, accept each new connection on the API worker with the fewest open connections, so requests are spread evenly across workers. Part of RFC #57479. This is an alternative to #58278 (SO_REUSEPORT listeners, and the accept-pacing rewrite on that branch) and builds on its accept loop.

## Claims

- Connections are spread evenly across API workers in bursts, when they arrive one at a time, and under overload. On main, one worker often takes most of a burst.
- RL `pause(mode="abort")` on GB200, DP2, 8 API servers: abort → all response bodies received goes from **40.0 s on main to 21.5 s** (Ao's accept pacing: 26.6 s; SO_REUSEPORT: 29.8 s).
- Ordinary serving with many short requests (Qwen3-0.6B, output length 1): **+43–85% requests/s** and lower TTFT than main, because on main a client's keep-alive pool lands on a few workers.
- A single API server is unchanged, and no new flags are added.

## Validation

**GPU: RL abort cycle.** GB200, Qwen3-0.6B, `--data-parallel-size 2 --api-server-count 8`, Python frontend.
- Workload: 128 concurrent non-streaming `/inference/v1/generate` requests, top-64 logprobs, `max_tokens` 32768; `POST /pause?mode=abort` after 25 s (about 670k aborted tokens, 2.5 GB of response bodies).
- Setup: the whole server is pinned to the GPUs' CPU socket (`taskset -c 70-139`). Without pinning, a worker that the scheduler moves between sockets mid-render adds 3–6 s of noise to any variant.
- Runs: 3 per variant in alternating order. All 128 responses were valid in every run. Connections per worker were counted with psutil just before the pause.

| variant | connections per worker (busiest … idlest) | abort → all bodies received | median |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | 31–34 … 5–8 | 39.2, 40.0, 43.0 s | 40.0 s |
| #58278 as reviewed (SO_REUSEPORT per worker) | 22–24 … 6–11 | 29.8, 28.1, 30.5 s | 29.8 s |
| accept one, then pause 1 ms (aoshen02 49dd8af1f5) | 19–20 … 12 | 26.6, 26.7, 24.3 s | 26.6 s |
| **this PR** | **16 on every worker, every run** | **21.4, 21.5, 21.7 s** | **21.5 s** |

Python workers render responses one at a time, so the busiest worker sets the tail. With this PR, all 8 workers finish within 0.9 s of each other.

**Short-request throughput** (requested in review). `vllm bench serve`, Qwen3-0.6B, random dataset, input 32 / output 1 tokens, `--ignore-eos --request-rate inf`, 30,000 requests per run after a 2,000-request warmup. Server pinned to the GPUs' CPU socket. 3 server starts per variant in alternating order; the PR is b9cae8206f and main is its base, 0f112d1800. All 36 runs had 0 failed requests.

| config | concurrency | main req/s (3 runs) | this PR req/s (3 runs) | change (median) | mean / p99 TTFT, main → PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DP2, 8 API servers | 64 | 1156, 1101, 1010 | 2042, 2041, 2085 | +85% | 57/81 → 30/39 ms |
| | 256 | 1625, 1556, 1573 | 2300, 2290, 2324 | +46% | 160/693 → 100/156 ms |
| | 1024 | 1446, 1462, 1493 | 2081, 2097, 2164 | +43% | 685/5014 → 427/673 ms |
| DP1, 4 API servers | 64 | 965, 975, 1198 | 1476, 1478, 1418 | +51% | 65/86 → 42/60 ms |
| | 256 | 1467, 1449, 1517 | 2163, 2220, 2169 | +48% | 171/308 → 110/200 ms |
| | 1024 | 1415, 1398, 1423 | 2169, 2113, 2139 | +51% | 703/1675 → 427/808 ms |

Why: the benchmark client opens its keep-alive pool in a burst, so on main a few workers take every connection. In a separate run of DP2 × 8 API servers at concurrency 64, connections per worker were [48, 15, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0] on main and 8 on each worker with this PR. Both variants are API-server-bound at this request size, so idle workers mean lost throughput.

<details>
<summary>CPU benchmark: connection distribution under different arrival patterns</summary>

Setup:
- 8 worker processes running vLLM's `NoSignalServer` on uvloop over one shared socket, exactly as `APIServerProcessManager` starts them, with a stub ASGI app.
- Each request waits for a hold time, then blocks the event loop for a render time.
- 5 runs each. Each cell shows the busiest worker's connection count against the fair share, then the tail after the last arrival.

| scenario | main | SO_REUSEPORT | accept pacing | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 256 at once, 50 ms render | 34–245 / 32, 10.6 s | 37–45, 2.07 s | 33–35, 1.71 s | 32, 1.62 s |
| 2000 at once, 5 ms render | 488–1850 / 250, 9.0 s | 263–287, 1.48 s | 254–262, 1.39 s | 250, 1.37 s |
| 512 over 2 s, 50 ms render (overloaded) | 148–193 / 64, 7.5 s | 74–78, 2.67 s | 99–146, 4.3 s | 65–74, 2.33 s |
| 500 over 5 s, 50 ms render (~60% CPU) | — | 70–80 / 63, 0.74 s | 78–108, 1.75 s | 68–70, 0.34 s |
| 5000 at once, no work (accept throughput) | 0.83 s | 0.49 s | 0.69 s | 0.55 s |

</details>

**Tests:** `tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_balanced_accepts.py` (new) checks:
- keep-alive requests are served on both asyncio and uvloop;
- a failed TLS handshake doesn't stop the accept loop;
- a busier worker still accepts when the least-loaded worker never does;
- 4 real worker processes × 400 connections, in a burst and spread over 1 s, end up within 1.25× of the fair share.

```
pytest tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_balanced_accepts.py \
       tests/entrypoints/launchers/api_server/ \
       tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_shutdown.py
```
Result: 28 passed on GB200, including the real multi-API-server shutdown tests. `pre-commit` (including the manual-stage mypy) is clean. CI already runs the new file through the `pytest entrypoints/launchers` step.

## Details

**Root cause.** All API workers inherit one listening socket. The event loop's own server accepts every queued connection on each wakeup, so whichever worker wakes first takes the whole burst. Connections that arrive one at a time tend to go to the most recently active worker.

**Design.**
- `APIServerProcessManager` shares one `RawArray("i")` slot per worker. This is the same mechanism as the existing `mp_admission_counters`.
- Each worker serves the shared socket with its own accept loop, instead of starting an asyncio server through uvicorn.
- When the socket becomes readable, a worker refreshes its own open-connection count and accepts only if it is the least loaded.
- Otherwise it rechecks every 1 ms, up to 5 times, then accepts anyway. That way a least-loaded worker that is blocked mid-render can't stall new connections.
- Accepted sockets go through uvicorn's own protocol via `loop.connect_accepted_socket`, each in its own task, so TLS handshakes don't hold up the accept loop. On shutdown, pending accepts and handshakes are cancelled; uvicorn already drains open connections.
- Slots start at INT32_MAX, so a worker that hasn't started is never chosen.

**Why not #58278.**
- SO_REUSEPORT gives each worker its own listener, and the kernel assigns connections by hash. That's random, and it clumps: about 25% over the fair share in bursts, and the 29.8 s tail above.
- Accept pacing (accept one connection, then pause 1 ms) balances bursts. With staggered arrivals the same worker keeps getting woken first, so some workers get no connections (99–146 on one worker against a fair share of 64 in the overloaded CPU case).

**Trade-offs.**
- Balancing has a cost: when every worker is busy rendering, short requests such as `/health` wait behind a render on whichever worker accepts them. In a mixed benchmark (the ~60% CPU case above plus `/health` polled at 100/s), `/health` p99 is about 50–100 ms with this PR, against under 1 ms with main or accept pacing, which leave some workers idle. SO_REUSEPORT is 0.6–1.9 s. When the CPU is overloaded, every balanced scheme sits around 1.5 s. A 20 ms recheck window doubled this cost for little extra balance, which is why the window is 5 ms. Faster rendering reduces both sides of this trade-off.
- It balances connections, not requests: a keep-alive client stays on its worker, as with any accept-level scheme.
- Every idle worker still wakes for each new connection, as on main.

---

</details>

**Not a duplicate:** the only open PR in this area is #58278. This PR takes a different approach and includes measurements of both variants of that PR.

@njhill thanks! Both inline comments are addressed in b9cae8206f:
- **Failed startup:** `startup` now returns early when the lifespan fails to start (only reachable on uvicorn < 0.50, which we still allow; reproduced on 0.48).

| DP2, 8 API servers | 64 | 1156, 1101, 1010 | 2042, 2041, 2085 | +85% | 57/81 → 30/39 ms |
| | 256 | 1625, 1556, 1573 | 2300, 2290, 2324 | +46% | 160/693 → 100/156 ms |

Most of the gain comes from how the client's keep-alive pool lands on the workers. `bench serve` opens its connections in a burst, so on main a few workers take all of them. ## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

If lifespan startup fails, `uvicorn.Server.startup()` returns early with `should_exit=True` and `started=False`, but this override carries on: it publishes a load of 0 (making this worker the most attractive target for peers), calls `listen()`, and starts the `_accept` tasks. `_serve()` then skips both `main_loop()` and `shutdown()` (the latter is gated on `self.started`), so nothing ever cancels those tasks and the worker keeps accepting connections onto an app that failed to start.

Suggest bailing out here:

```suggestion
        await super().startup(sockets=[])
        if not self.started:
            return
```

@@ -34,23 +34,138 @@
 
 logger = init_logger(__name__)
 
+# A worker with more connections than another leaves a pending connection to
+# the less loaded one, rechecking every 1 ms, for up to 5 ms (it may be busy).
+_ACCEPT_DEFER_CHECKS = 5
+
 
 class NoSignalServer(uvicorn.Server):
     """Uvicorn server that never installs its own SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers.
 
     Callers register their own handlers on the event loop for graceful
     shutdown; uvicorn's would race with and override them (see #49668).
+
+    With ``peer_loads`` (several API workers on one shared socket: a shared
+    array with one slot per worker, and this worker's index), each worker
+    publishes its number of open connections, and a pending connection is
+    accepted by the least loaded worker. The event loop's own server would
+    accept every queued connection in whichever worker wakes first.
     """
 
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        config: uvicorn.Config,
+        peer_loads: tuple[MutableSequence[int], int] | None = None,
+    ):
+        super().__init__(config)
+        self.peer_loads = peer_loads
+        self._accept_tasks: set[asyncio.Task] = set()
+        self._connecting = 0
+
     @contextlib.contextmanager
     def capture_signals(self) -> Generator[None, None, None]:
         yield
 
+    def _publish_load(self) -> None:
+        assert self.peer_loads is not None
+        loads, index = self.peer_loads
+        loads[index] = len(self.server_state.connections) + self._connecting
+
+    def _least_loaded(self) -> bool:
+        assert self.peer_loads is not None
+        loads, index = self.peer_loads
+        return loads[index] <= min(loads)
+
+    async def startup(self, sockets: list[socket.socket] | None = None) -> None:
+        if not (self.peer_loads and sockets):
+            return await super().startup(sockets)
+        # With no sockets uvicorn starts no asyncio server; _accept serves
+        # them with uvicorn's protocol instead.
+        await super().startup(sockets=[])

nodes.body:
The accept tasks are cancelled but not awaited, and `super().shutdown()` closes the listening socket synchronously (before its first `await`). So the cancellation is only delivered afterwards, and `_readable`'s `finally: loop.remove_reader(sock)` runs against an already-closed socket. uvloop tolerates this (its io-ref on the socket defers the real close), and stdlib asyncio only gets by via the selector's exhaustive-search fallback, with the closed fd still registered in the meantime.

Suggest awaiting the cancelled tasks before handing off, e.g.:

```python
        tasks = list(self._accept_tasks)
        for task in tasks:
            task.cancel()
        await asyncio.gather(*tasks, return_exceptions=True)
        await super().shutdown(sockets)
```

Related nit: the slot in `peer_loads` is never reset on shutdown, so a stopped worker keeps advertising its last count. Setting it back to `2**31 - 1` here would match the "not started" sentinel.

     """
 
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        config: uvicorn.Config,
+        peer_loads: tuple[MutableSequence[int], int] | None = None,
+    ):
+        super().__init__(config)
+        self.peer_loads = peer_loads
+        self._accept_tasks: set[asyncio.Task] = set()
+        self._connecting = 0
+
     @contextlib.contextmanager
     def capture_signals(self) -> Generator[None, None, None]:
         yield
 
+    def _publish_load(self) -> None:
+        assert self.peer_loads is not None
+        loads, index = self.peer_loads
+        loads[index] = len(self.server_state.connections) + self._connecting
+
+    def _least_loaded(self) -> bool:
+        assert self.peer_loads is not None
+        loads, index = self.peer_loads
+        return loads[index] <= min(loads)
+
+    async def startup(self, sockets: list[socket.socket] | None = None) -> None:
+        if not (self.peer_loads and sockets):
+            return await super().startup(sockets)
+        # With no sockets uvicorn starts no asyncio server; _accept serves
+        # them with uvicorn's protocol instead.
+        await super().startup(sockets=[])
+        self._publish_load()
+        for sock in sockets:
+            sock.listen(self.config.backlog)
+            sock.setblocking(False)
+            self._track(self._accept(sock))
+
+    def _track(self, coro) -> None:
+        task = asyncio.create_task(coro)
+        self._accept_tasks.add(task)
+        task.add_done_callback(self._accept_tasks.discard)
+
+    async def _accept(self, sock: socket.socket) -> None:
+        loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
+        while True:
+            await _readable(loop, sock)
+            # Connections closed since the last accept; peers refresh likewise.
+            self._publish_load()
+            for _ in range(_ACCEPT_DEFER_CHECKS):
+                if self._least_loaded():
+                    break
+                await asyncio.sleep(0.001)
+            try:
+                conn, _ = sock.accept()
+            except (BlockingIOError, InterruptedError, ConnectionAbortedError):
+                continue  # another worker took it
+            except OSError:
+                # e.g. EMFILE; asyncio's own server also retries after 1 s.
+                logger.exception("Error accepting a connection")
+                await asyncio.sleep(1)
+                continue
+            self._connecting += 1
+            self._publish_load()
+            # Its own task, so a TLS handshake does not hold up the next accept.
+            self._track(self._connect(loop, conn))
+
+    async def _connect(self, loop: asyncio.AbstractEventLoop, conn: socket.socket):
+        config = self.config
+        try:
+            await loop.connect_accepted_socket(
+                lambda: config.http_protocol_class(  # type: ignore[call-arg]
+                    config=config,
+                    server_state=self.server_state,
+                    app_state=self.lifespan.state,
+                    _loop=loop,
+                ),
+                conn,
+                ssl=config.ssl,
+            )
+        except asyncio.CancelledError:
+            conn.close()
+            raise
+        except Exception:
+            # e.g. a failed TLS handshake
+            logger.debug("Accepted connection failed to start", exc_info=True)
+            conn.close()
+        finally:
+            self._connecting -= 1
+            self._publish_load()
+
+    async def shutdown(self, sockets: list[socket.socket] | None = None) -> None:
+        for task in list(self._accept_tasks):
+            task.cancel()
+        await super().shutdown(sockets)

Result: 28 passed on GB200, including the real multi-API-server shutdown tests. `pre-commit` (including the manual-stage mypy) is clean. CI already runs the new file through the `pytest entrypoints/launchers` step.

## Details

**Root cause.** All API workers inherit one listening socket. The event loop's own server accepts every queued connection on each wakeup, so whichever worker wakes first takes the whole burst. Connections that arrive one at a time tend to go to the most recently active worker.

**Design.**
- `APIServerProcessManager` shares one `RawArray("i")` slot per worker. This is the same mechanism as the existing `mp_admission_counters`.
- Each worker serves the shared socket with its own accept loop, instead of starting an asyncio server through uvicorn.
- When the socket becomes readable, a worker refreshes its own open-connection count and accepts only if it is the least loaded.
- Otherwise it rechecks every 1 ms, up to 5 times, then accepts anyway. That way a least-loaded worker that is blocked mid-render can't stall new connections.
- Accepted sockets go through uvicorn's own protocol via `loop.connect_accepted_socket`, each in its own task, so TLS handshakes don't hold up the accept loop. On shutdown, pending accepts and handshakes are cancelled; uvicorn already drains open connections.
- Slots start at INT32_MAX, so a worker that hasn't started is never chosen.

**Why not #58278.**
- SO_REUSEPORT gives each worker its own listener, and the kernel assigns connections by hash. That's random, and it clumps: about 25% over the fair share in bursts, and the 29.8 s tail above.
- Accept pacing (accept one connection, then pause 1 ms) balances bursts. With staggered arrivals the same worker keeps getting woken first, so some workers get no connections (99–146 on one worker against a fair share of 64 in the overloaded CPU case).

**Trade-offs.**
- Balancing has a cost: when every worker is busy rendering, short requests such as `/health` wait behind a render on whichever worker accepts them. In a mixed benchmark (the ~60% CPU case above plus `/health` polled at 100/s), `/health` p99 is about 50–100 ms with this PR, against under 1 ms with main or accept pacing, which leave some workers idle. SO_REUSEPORT is 0.6–1.9 s. When the CPU is overloaded, every balanced scheme sits around 1.5 s. A 20 ms recheck window doubled this cost for little extra balance, which is why the window is 5 ms. Faster rendering reduces both sides of this trade-off.
- It balances connections, not requests: a keep-alive client stays on its worker, as with any accept-level scheme.
- Every idle worker still wakes for each new connection, as on main.

+"""NoSignalServer(peer_loads=...): API workers sharing one listening socket
+accept each connection on the worker with the fewest open connections."""

+import asyncio
+import datetime
+import multiprocessing
+import os
+import socket
+import ssl

+import pytest
+import uvicorn
+import uvloop
+
+from vllm.entrypoints.launchers.launcher import NoSignalServer
+
+TIMEOUT_S = 30
+
+
+def _bound_socket() -> socket.socket:
+    # Like setup_server: bound, not yet listening.
+    sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
+    sock.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
+    sock.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
+    return sock
+
+
+def _app(hold_s: float = 0.0):
+    pid = str(os.getpid()).encode()
+
+    async def app(scope, receive, send):
+        if scope["type"] == "lifespan":
+            while (await receive())["type"] != "lifespan.shutdown":
+                await send({"type": "lifespan.startup.complete"})
+            await send({"type": "lifespan.shutdown.complete"})
+            return
+        await asyncio.sleep(hold_s)
+        headers = [(b"content-length", str(len(pid)).encode())]
+        await send({"type": "http.response.start", "status": 200, "headers": headers})
+        await send({"type": "http.response.body", "body": pid})
+
+    return app
+
+
+async def _get(port: int, requests: int = 1, ssl_ctx=None) -> list[bytes]:
+    """``requests`` requests on one keep-alive connection; returns the bodies."""
+    reader, writer = await asyncio.open_connection("127.0.0.1", port, ssl=ssl_ctx)
+    bodies = []
+    for _ in range(requests):
+        writer.write(b"GET / HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: t\r\n\r\n")
+        head = await asyncio.wait_for(reader.readuntil(b"\r\n\r\n"), TIMEOUT_S)
+        assert head.startswith(b"HTTP/1.1 200")
+        length = int(head.split(b"content-length: ")[1].split(b"\r\n")[0])
+        bodies.append(await asyncio.wait_for(reader.readexactly(length), TIMEOUT_S))
+    writer.close()
+    return bodies
+
+
+async def _serve(sock, requests, loads=None, **config_kwargs):
+    config = uvicorn.Config(_app(), lifespan="on", log_level="warning", **config_kwargs)
+    loads = loads if loads is not None else [0]
+    server = NoSignalServer(config, peer_loads=(loads, 0))
+    task = asyncio.create_task(server.serve(sockets=[sock]))
+    while not server.started:
+        assert not task.done(), task.result()
+        await asyncio.sleep(0.01)
+    try:
+        return await requests(sock.getsockname()[1], server)
+    finally:
+        server.should_exit = True
+        await asyncio.wait_for(task, TIMEOUT_S)
+        # The listener is closed, nothing is left accepting, and peers no
+        # longer see this worker as a target.
+        assert sock.fileno() == -1
+        assert not server._accept_tasks
+        assert loads[0] == 2**31 - 1
+

+def _run(coro, loop_impl):
+    return uvloop.run(coro) if loop_impl == "uvloop" else asyncio.run(coro)

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("loop_impl", ["asyncio", "uvloop"])

+    assert one == [str(os.getpid()).encode()]
+    assert len(three) == 3

+def _self_signed(tmp_path):

+    )

+    client_ctx.verify_mode = ssl.CERT_NONE

+        reader, writer = await asyncio.open_connection("127.0.0.1", port)
+        writer.write(b"GET / HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: t\r\n\r\n")
+        await asyncio.wait_for(reader.read(), TIMEOUT_S)
+        writer.close()
+        return await _get(port, ssl_ctx=client_ctx)
+
+    bodies = uvloop.run(
+        _serve(_bound_socket(), requests, ssl_keyfile=keyfile, ssl_certfile=certfile)
+    )
+    assert bodies == [str(os.getpid()).encode()]
+
+
+def test_busier_worker_still_serves():
+    # This worker is index 0; peer 1 claims no connections but never accepts.
+    loads = [0, 0]
+
+    async def requests(port, server):
+        reader, writer = await asyncio.open_connection("127.0.0.1", port)
+        bodies = await _get(port)
+        assert loads[0] >= 1  # the held connection was published
+        writer.close()
+        return bodies
+
+    assert uvloop.run(_serve(_bound_socket(), requests, loads)) == [
+        str(os.getpid()).encode()

+
+
+def _worker(sock, loads, index, ready, stop):
+    async def main():
+        config = uvicorn.Config(_app(hold_s=1), lifespan="on", log_level="warning")
+        server = NoSignalServer(config, peer_loads=(loads, index))
+        task = asyncio.create_task(server.serve(sockets=[sock]))
+        while not server.started:
+            await asyncio.sleep(0.01)
+        ready.release()
+        await asyncio.get_running_loop().run_in_executor(None, stop.wait)
+        server.should_exit = True
+        await task
+
+    # API workers run on uvloop, whose own server accepts a whole burst at once.
+    uvloop.run(main())
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif((os.cpu_count() or 1) < 8, reason="needs idle cores per worker")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("arrival_s", [0, 1])
+def test_connections_balanced_over_workers(arrival_s):
+    """Both a burst and a steady stream of connections end up balanced; with
+    the event loop's own server one worker takes most of either."""
+    workers, connections = 4, 400
+    sock = _bound_socket()
+    ctx = multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")
+    ready, stop = ctx.Semaphore(0), ctx.Event()
+    loads = ctx.RawArray("i", workers)
+    procs = [
+        ctx.Process(target=_worker, args=(sock, loads, i, ready, stop))
+        for i in range(workers)
+    ]
+    for p in procs:
+        p.start()
+    try:
+        for _ in range(workers):
+            assert ready.acquire(timeout=120)
+
+        async def get_after(delay):
+            await asyncio.sleep(delay)
+            return await _get(sock.getsockname()[1])
+
+        async def arrive():
+            delays = [arrival_s * i / connections for i in range(connections)]
+            results = await asyncio.gather(*(get_after(d) for d in delays))
+            return Counter(body for (body,) in results)
+
+        counts = uvloop.run(arrive())
+        assert sum(counts.values()) == connections
+        # Fair share is 100.
+        assert max(counts.values()) <= 5 * connections // (4 * workers), counts
+    finally:
+        stop.set()
+        for p in procs:
+            p.join(30)
+            if p.is_alive():
+                p.kill()
+        sock.close()

If lifespan startup fails, `uvicorn.Server.startup()` returns early with `should_exit=True` and `started=False`, but this override carries on: it publishes a load of 0 (making this worker the most attractive target for peers), calls `listen()`, and starts the `_accept` tasks. `_serve()` then skips both `main_loop()` and `shutdown()` (the latter is gated on `self.started`), so nothing ever cancels those tasks and the worker keeps accepting connections onto an app that failed to start.

Suggest bailing out here:

```suggestion
        await super().startup(sockets=[])
        if not self.started:
            return
```

inline_comments.body:
The accept tasks are cancelled but not awaited, and `super().shutdown()` closes the listening socket synchronously (before its first `await`). So the cancellation is only delivered afterwards, and `_readable`'s `finally: loop.remove_reader(sock)` runs against an already-closed socket. uvloop tolerates this (its io-ref on the socket defers the real close), and stdlib asyncio only gets by via the selector's exhaustive-search fallback, with the closed fd still registered in the meantime.

Suggest awaiting the cancelled tasks before handing off, e.g.:

```python
        tasks = list(self._accept_tasks)
        for task in tasks:
            task.cancel()
        await asyncio.gather(*tasks, return_exceptions=True)
        await super().shutdown(sockets)
```

Related nit: the slot in `peer_loads` is never reset on shutdown, so a stopped worker keeps advertising its last count. Setting it back to `2**31 - 1` here would match the "not started" sentinel.

+    accept every queued connection in whichever worker wakes first.
     """
 
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        config: uvicorn.Config,
+        peer_loads: tuple[MutableSequence[int], int] | None = None,
+    ):
+        super().__init__(config)
+        self.peer_loads = peer_loads
+        self._accept_tasks: set[asyncio.Task] = set()
+        self._connecting = 0
+
     @contextlib.contextmanager
     def capture_signals(self) -> Generator[None, None, None]:
         yield
 
+    def _publish_load(self) -> None:
+        assert self.peer_loads is not None
+        loads, index = self.peer_loads
+        loads[index] = len(self.server_state.connections) + self._connecting
+
+    def _least_loaded(self) -> bool:
+        assert self.peer_loads is not None
+        loads, index = self.peer_loads
+        return loads[index] <= min(loads)
+
+    async def startup(self, sockets: list[socket.socket] | None = None) -> None:
+        if not (self.peer_loads and sockets):
+            return await super().startup(sockets)
+        # With no sockets uvicorn starts no asyncio server; _accept serves
+        # them with uvicorn's protocol instead.
+        await super().startup(sockets=[])
+        self._publish_load()
+        for sock in sockets:
+            sock.listen(self.config.backlog)
+            sock.setblocking(False)
+            self._track(self._accept(sock))
+
+    def _track(self, coro) -> None:
+        task = asyncio.create_task(coro)
+        self._accept_tasks.add(task)
+        task.add_done_callback(self._accept_tasks.discard)
+
+    async def _accept(self, sock: socket.socket) -> None:
+        loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
+        while True:
+            await _readable(loop, sock)
+            # Connections closed since the last accept; peers refresh likewise.
+            self._publish_load()
+            for _ in range(_ACCEPT_DEFER_CHECKS):
+                if self._least_loaded():
+                    break
+                await asyncio.sleep(0.001)
+            try:
+                conn, _ = sock.accept()
+            except (BlockingIOError, InterruptedError, ConnectionAbortedError):
+                continue  # another worker took it
+            except OSError:
+                # e.g. EMFILE; asyncio's own server also retries after 1 s.
+                logger.exception("Error accepting a connection")
+                await asyncio.sleep(1)
+                continue
+            self._connecting += 1
+            self._publish_load()
+            # Its own task, so a TLS handshake does not hold up the next accept.
+            self._track(self._connect(loop, conn))
+
+    async def _connect(self, loop: asyncio.AbstractEventLoop, conn: socket.socket):
+        config = self.config
+        try:
+            await loop.connect_accepted_socket(
+                lambda: config.http_protocol_class(  # type: ignore[call-arg]
+                    config=config,
+                    server_state=self.server_state,
+                    app_state=self.lifespan.state,
+                    _loop=loop,
+                ),
+                conn,
+                ssl=config.ssl,
+            )
+        except asyncio.CancelledError:
+            conn.close()
+            raise
+        except Exception:
+            # e.g. a failed TLS handshake
+            logger.debug("Accepted connection failed to start", exc_info=True)
+            conn.close()
+        finally:
+            self._connecting -= 1
+            self._publish_load()
+
+    async def shutdown(self, sockets: list[socket.socket] | None = None) -> None:
+        for task in list(self._accept_tasks):
+            task.cancel()
+        await super().shutdown(sockets)

@hao-aaron actually only other thought is to do some before/after throughput tests on a very small model with a high volume of short requests (e.g. short ISL and OSL=1).

I just mean regular serving load, not the abort test.

@njhill thanks! Both inline comments are addressed in b9cae8206f:
- **Failed startup:** `startup` now returns early when the lifespan fails to start (only reachable on uvicorn < 0.50, which we still allow; reproduced on 0.48).
- **Shutdown:** the cancelled accept tasks are now awaited before `super().shutdown()` closes the socket.
- **The nit:** the slot is reset to the "not started" value afterwards.

**Short-request throughput:** `vllm bench serve`, Qwen3-0.6B, random dataset, input 32 / output 1 tokens, `--ignore-eos --request-rate inf`, 30,000 requests per run after a 2,000-request warmup. Server pinned to the GPUs' CPU socket; 3 server starts per variant in alternating order. Main is 0f112d1800 (the base of this PR). All 36 runs had 0 failed requests.

| config | concurrency | main req/s | this PR req/s | change (median) | mean / p99 TTFT, main → PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DP2, 8 API servers | 64 | 1156, 1101, 1010 | 2042, 2041, 2085 | +85% | 57/81 → 30/39 ms |
| | 256 | 1625, 1556, 1573 | 2300, 2290, 2324 | +46% | 160/693 → 100/156 ms |
| | 1024 | 1446, 1462, 1493 | 2081, 2097, 2164 | +43% | 685/5014 → 427/673 ms |
| DP1, 4 API servers | 64 | 965, 975, 1198 | 1476, 1478, 1418 | +51% | 65/86 → 42/60 ms |
| | 256 | 1467, 1449, 1517 | 2163, 2220, 2169 | +48% | 171/308 → 110/200 ms |
| | 1024 | 1415, 1398, 1423 | 2169, 2113, 2139 | +51% | 703/1675 → 427/808 ms |

Most of the gain comes from how the client's keep-alive pool lands on the workers. `bench serve` opens its connections in a burst, so on main a few workers take all of them. At DP2 × 8 API servers and concurrency 64, connections per worker were [48, 15, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0] on main and 8 on every worker with this PR. At this request size both variants are API-server-bound, so the idle workers are lost throughput. A client that opens connections gradually, or a load balancer with its own pool, would likely see a smaller gap.
